arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argued judges need discretion to impose just sentences.
The government argued the statute mandates a specific consecutive term.
Justice Sotomayor questioned if a one-day sentence satisfies the law.
Justice Kagan questioned if a one-day sentence defeats the mandate.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case involves a defendant who received a mandatory 30-year sentence. He argues the judge should have discretion to reduce it. The government argues the statute requires the full term.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to allow judges to reduce mandatory sentences.
The government wants the Court to enforce the mandatory 30-year sentence.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues judges must have discretion to ensure just results.
The government argues Congress intended to remove judicial discretion for these crimes.
